newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up across the curve as next winter firms.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up across the curve as next winter firms.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices continued to firm across the forward curve on Thursday with winter quarters Q4, Q1 and Q2 seeing the bulk of activity and the price increases, traders and brokers said.
The market was quiet and lethargic in the morning with a few within-day and day ahead trades getting done but little activity for longer periods.
Late in the morning a Q2 deal was done at 11.25 pence a therm, and then the market started to rally after lunch.

A spate of trades followed in the afternoon, with Q4, Q1, Q2 and the Q1/Q2 strip all trading several times. There were rumours that the gas year from October had also traded but this was not confirmed.
Unlike Wednesday's market, when traders said prices were driven up by a single buyer actively buying Q1, there was good interest from both buyers and sellers.
"There's definitely buying support but there are quite a few players selling as well so it's traded it's way up," said a trader. "There's a definite firming of numbers."
He added that with a few more players active in the market than on Wednesday, offers had started to go back up, so sending prices higher.

Another trader said he suspected there were a lot of deals, especially in the second quarter, that were not getting made public. "There's more going on here than is getting reported, probably," he said. "There's some front-running by buyers that's made it run up a bit quicker, but there's some genuine buying as well," he added.

A trade in the first quarter at St Fergus was done at 15.50 pence a therm. The seller said pipeline capacity from St Fergus was trading at around 0.80 pence a therm in the fourth quarter, and he believed capacity was worth between 0.90 pence and 1.0 pence a therm in the first quarter. This would give the gas an equivalent value of a little over 16.40 pence at the NBP, in line with the top end of the prices achieved there.

There was as usual a reasonable volume of trade done on the prompt market, with within-day, day ahead and weekend gas all trading. But with the exception of a single deal for September, all the rest of the trade was for either quarters or groups of quarters, continuing a recent trend in this direction.

IPE futures were firmer in line with developments on the physical market. 125 lots were traded in August, October and January. The biggest gains were in January which rose by 0.225 pence a therm to trade and settle at 17.40 pence a therm, consistent with the rises seen on the OTC market.
